Chapter 222: 0219 Peking University Alumni Entrepreneurship Forum

At noon, it was time to get off work.

All the employees wore masks, and the company’s windows were all tightly shut.

Chen Guiliang left the company half an hour before the other employees. Most of the people he met downstairs were wearing masks.

After having lunch at the first-floor cafeteria, Chen Guiliang went out to ride his bike back to the dorm.

His bicycle, parked downstairs from the company, was already covered in a layer of dust.

The sky was a bit dim.

As early as during the financing negotiations, Beijing had been frequently hit by sandstorms. This was already the 12th sand-and-dust weather event since the beginning of spring!

Chen Guiliang took out a cloth to wipe the dust off his bike seat, then lifted the bike and shook it repeatedly a few times. He could still feel the sandy grating sound from the wheel hubs as he rode.

Everywhere he looked along the way, there was dust.

He returned to the dorm building, parked his bike, and locked it.

He saw a crowd of students gathered in front of the building, and his counselor, Senior Brother Long Xiang, was also there.

A first-year master's student in Environmental Engineering was on the ground, drawing a simple map and explaining, "The newspapers and the internet are all abuzz right now about why our country's Three-North Shelterbelt Program, which we've invested a huge amount of money in, isn't showing any results. Some people even question if the money was embezzled..."

"In the middle of last month, a total of 330,000 tons of floating dust fell on Beijing within two days. Many media outlets call it a sandstorm, but to be precise, it should be called a 'dust storm.' Sand particles and dust particles are different. Floating dust can rise into the stratosphere and travel. No shelterbelt can block it at an altitude of several thousand meters..."

"Through particle size analysis, the main source of this dust storm is dry salt lakes... The expansion of dry salt lake areas in the grasslands and northwestern Hebei Province is mainly caused by human factors. Damming rivers upstream and blindly expanding irrigation areas have caused the lakes to gradually dry up... These dry salt lakes form a hardpan surface. The drastic temperature changes between day and night in spring and summer cause intense frost heaving and freeze-thaw cycles. Eventually, the hardpan surface of the dry salt lakes breaks up, forming soft, saline-alkali dust material..."

"In recent years, the rate at which the remaining saltwater lakes on our country's grasslands are drying up has clearly accelerated. On average, 20 natural lakes disappear every year..."

"So, if we want to eradicate the sandstorm weather in Beijing, we must start from the source on the grasslands. We need to tear down those upstream dams and turn the farmland back into grasslands..."

The students listened carefully to this senior's explanation and finally had a moment of realization.

"Clap, clap, clap!"

Applause rang out.

Chen Guiliang also joined in the applause.

That first-year master's senior said with passionate indignation, "In the second half of the year, I will follow my advisor to the grasslands to conduct in-depth research. If I can't get the dry salt lakes under control, I'll live on the grasslands for the rest of my life!"

"Hear, hear!"

"Go, Senior Brother!"

The students cheered loudly.

That senior clasped his hands in a fist-and-palm salute, like a chivalrous hero from the martial arts world, and bid farewell to the crowd.

Amidst the passion, there was also a touch of tragic heroism.

In reality, the first phase of the Beijing-Tianjin Sandstorm Source Control Project had already been launched four years ago. It involved work on many different fronts, especially the need to solve the basic survival problems of the local people.

It wasn't as simple as just saying you'd return farmland to its original state!

The scope of the control project was continuously expanding. This senior brother was part of the third batch heading to the grasslands. Traveling with them were also experts and graduate students in agriculture and animal husbandry.

After the first-year master's student left, Chen Guiliang asked Long Xiang, "Why did a graduate student come all the way over here?"

Long Xiang said, "He's a senior from the first class of the Yuanpei Program. I invited him to give a talk and let the junior students get a glimpse of their senior's impressive demeanor."

"Senior Brother Long, have you decided to stay at the university?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Long Xiang replied, "I was already confirmed for postgraduate admission exemption last semester."

"Congratulations, congratulations," Chen Guiliang said, genuinely unaware.

"I should be the one congratulating you. You're getting more and more awesome," Long Xiang said, then asked, "I heard you're going to speak at some Peking University Alumni Entrepreneurship Forum?"

Chen Guiliang said, "This afternoon at three."

Long Xiang said, "It doesn't require a ticket, does it?"

"No, just go early to get a seat," Chen Guiliang said.

"Then I have to go join in the fun," Long Xiang said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang went back to his dorm for a nap. After being woken by his alarm clock, he pedaled his bike over to the Centennial Hall.

President Xu didn't come.

The highest-ranking official present was Peking University's Deputy Secretary, Deputy Director of University Affairs, General Counsel, and Dean of the Guanghua School of Management, Dean Wu.

There were a good five or six alumni entrepreneurs who had achieved success.

Li Yanhong, Ding Jian, Yu Hongmin, and the like... none of them came today!

Wang Zhidong, the founder of Sina, was currently chatting with Dean Wu. The other entrepreneur alumni were also chatting amongst themselves.

"Haha, President Chen is here," Dean Wu said in a joking tone.

Those few alumni smiled and stood up to shake hands with Chen Guiliang.

Wang Zhidong had long been kicked out of Sina. He took the opportunity to promote his current product, trying to persuade Chen Guiliang's two companies to use his enterprise instant messaging tool.

This thing was for internal communication among company employees only, and it was more secure and practical than QQ and MSN.

Chen Guiliang didn't agree immediately, planning to try it out for a period first.

The two sides immediately reached a verbal agreement: ByteDance and Game Science would have a free three-month trial of Wang Zhidong's enterprise communication software.

With a business collaboration in place, their relationship was instantly closer.

Wang Zhidong voluntarily stated that he would join Hainei and Kaixin and activate the mobile microblog function.

Just then, a man wearing glasses appeared.

Dangdang's Li Guoqin...

Chen Guiliang felt like laughing the moment he saw this person, involuntarily thinking of the "high-level business warfare" meme.

This guy later had a falling out with his wife, and stormed the company with several burly directors, the board secretary, a cameraman, an assistant, an administrative staffer, and a driver, snatching the official and financial seals.

His wife chose to report it directly to the police and declared that any documents stamped with those seals would no longer have legal effect.

Li Guoqin, on the other hand, announced that he would personally keep these company seals until a new seal management policy was established. He even said he would tie the seals to his belt during the day and sleep with them in his bed at night.

It was quite surreal.

After exchanging pleasantries with Dean Wu, Li Guoqin enthusiastically shook hands with Wang Zhidong, "Haha, Old Wang, long time no see!"

After some small talk, he came over to shake hands with Chen Guiliang, "Junior Brother Chen's novels and Legend of the Three Kingdoms are selling extremely well on our Dangdang."

"Thank you for your help, Senior Brother," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Guoqin said, "We're all alumni, we should cooperate closely. We can all make money together!"

Next, Li Guoqin went to shake hands with the other alumni entrepreneurs.

It was about time, and everyone headed to the forum venue.

The place was already packed, with students crowding the aisles as well.

Dean Wu spoke first, "Some media outlets say that this year, China has entered an era of 'crazy-vesting.' The 'crazy' as in 'insane.' Many faculty and students are getting restless, discussing how to start a business. Some have even taken action. From the beginning of March until now, the incubator company at the Science Park has already received dozens of startup applications..."

"Starting a business is a major undertaking, it cannot be done blindly... So, today we've invited some successful alumni entrepreneurs to share their startup experiences..."

On the stage, there were several chairs arranged in a crescent shape.

Wang Zhidong naturally sat in the center seat.

For the other center seat, everyone deferred to one another. In the end, Li Guoqin sat down with a grin, constantly clasping his hands in a fist-and-palm salute to the others, expressing that it would be disrespectful to refuse.

Wang Zhidong picked up the microphone and said, "Seventeen years ago, I was doing development work at Peking University Founder Group, and I independently developed the country's first practical Windows 3.0. Later, I developed some other software... As you all know, Sina kicked me, the founder, out. I only found out when I read the newspaper that I had already resigned from Sina."

"Hahahaha!"

A wave of laughter erupted from the audience.

Wang Zhidong continued, "If any of you here want to start a business, I only have two pieces of advice. First, get familiar with the specific business first. Don't start a company without understanding anything. Second, keep a firm grip on the control of the company, lest you find out from the newspaper one day that you've resigned."

"Hahaha!"

Another round of laughter ensued.

Mainly because that line was too funny, just like how J.K. Rowling was later "excommunicated from the Harry Potter fandom" by fans.

Li Guoqin picked up the microphone and said, "I very much agree with President Wang's advice. I was already in the book publishing industry for ten years before I founded Dangdang. Later, I just moved the business of selling books from offline to online. Why was Dangdang able to stand out from so many competitors? Because I know more about selling books than they do, and I already had mature supply channels."

"If any students or teachers here want to start a business, you might as well go into a traditional industry first, and then combine that traditional industry with the internet. That way, your internet company will be different from others. You'll have your own advantages and selling points. This is very important, and venture capitalists really like it."

The third speaker was Lei Ming, "When Baidu was first founded, I was in charge of technology. I learned a lot and had many insights. Of the so-called Seven Swordsmen of Baidu, I was the first to leave... Now that I've founded Kuwo Music, my ability to carve out a path is mainly due to product technology innovation. The market is important, but technology is also important. As long as you have unique technology, your market performance won't be too bad..."

Finally, it was Chen Guiliang's turn, "The words of the three senior brothers have taught me a lot. My experience is simple. I chose the right trend on the internet, and I was instantly blown up to the sky. Choosing a startup project is the most important thing, otherwise, no amount of effort will be of any use..."

"Of course, you also need to be strategic. Take Kaixin as an example. Why did I use that name at the beginning? Because 'Kaixin' (happy) was more conducive to early-stage promotion. Now I've changed it to Hainei, which is beneficial for the website's future development. As early as when I registered Xiaonei, I had already registered the trademark and domain name for Hainei at the same time..."

"I'm not clear about other fields, but in the area of SNS websites, I don't recommend everyone choose it as a startup project. The competition is too fierce. Even communities like Mop have started to launch 'space' features. Sina Blog is also developing towards an SNS website... This is a red ocean where corpses litter the battlefield."

The fifth speaker was Chen Hua, "President Chen of ByteDance is absolutely right, and I can add one more point. Many internet companies in various fields have already grown large, so latecomers have to focus on niche markets. That being said, what should we, who are in the search business, do? We can only deeply cultivate vertical and niche markets, so I'm doing train ticket booking search, and travel search..."

After everyone had spoken one by one, the group began to chat and discuss.

(Facepalm) Please give...
